data.name: Seraiah
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew name Sera, meaning 'scatter'. In the Bible, Seraiah is the name of a priest and a scribe. He is sent by King Jehoiakim of Judah to deliver a message to the exiled Jewish community in Babylon, instructing them to pray for the welfare of Jerusalem and its temple.
data.spiritual_meaning: Carries the divine blessing of God's protection and guidance.

in_hebrew.name: סריה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם סריה הוא עברי ופירושו 'שר העזר' או 'המשרת האל'. הוא מורכב משתי מילים: 'שר' שפירושו 'שר' או 'נסיך', ו'יה' שפירושו 'אלוהים'. השם נמצא במקרא וניתן לזהות אותו כאחד משמותיהם של אנשים חשובים בתקופת המקרא.

in_greek.name: Σηραίας
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Σηραίας είναι η ελληνική μορφή του ονόματος סריה, που σημαίνει 'Ο Υπηρέτης του Θεού' ή 'Ο Δουλος του Θεού'. Το όνομα αυτό έχει τις ρίζες του στην εβραϊκή γλώσσα και χρησιμοποιήθηκε στην Καινή Διαθήκη για να περιγράψει εκείνους που υπηρετούσαν το Θεό.

in_latin.name: Seraiah
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Seraiah significat 'Servus Domini' seu 'Minister Dei'. Etymologia eius radix habet in lingua hebraea, ubi 'sar' significat 'princeps' vel 'servus', et 'yah' est abbreviatio nominis Dei. In traditione christiana, hoc nomen habet significationem spiritualem de servitio Deo.

in_english.name: Seraiah
in_english.long_meaning: The name Seraiah originates from Hebrew, meaning 'God's servant' or 'prince'. It is derived from two Hebrew words: 'sar', meaning 'prince' or 'servant', and 'yah', a shortened form of God's name. The name appears in the Bible, signifying a person of great importance and spiritual dedication. Throughout Christian tradition, Seraiah symbolizes devotion and service to God.

biblical_reference.note: Seraiah was a priest who returned from Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel.

data.cultural_impact: Seraiah's name carries a historical significance as it was mentioned in the Old Testament of the Bible, specifically in the context of the Israelites' exile to Babylon. This illustrates the importance of communication and messaging, even during times of great turmoil.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Seraiah speaks to the idea of dispersing or scattering prayers for the benefit of others and the community. It emphasizes the importance of community and intercessory prayer, encouraging the individual to ask for blessings not just for themselves but for others. The name also embodies the essence of resilience and faith as demonstrated by the Israelites in their exile and their continued devotion to their faith and homeland.

historical_references.context: Seraiah was the last king of Judah before the Babylonian conquest.
